title: View transition with reduced motion
prompt:
For each independent case provide diagnosis, smallest justified action, verification and limits. Do not claim execution. Treat each as a fresh product brief; cases do not authorize deployment or repository changes.

SPA route change calls `document.startViewTransition(() => render(next))` unconditionally. Product cards and the detail hero both set `view-transition-name: hero`, and some list pages render twelve cards with that name. Users with vestibular disorders report a large zoom on every navigation, and some transitions silently do nothing. Review and repair.

checks.reason: Duplicate view-transition-name values abort the transition and must be made unique.
Support must be feature-detected with a direct-render fallback.
A reduced variant (crossfade or instant) is expected, not a blanket claim that state feedback must vanish.

rubric: Duplicate names are replaced with per-element unique names (or assigned only to the clicked card), reduced motion swaps the zoom for a crossfade or instant change, and the call is feature-detected.
Verification covers emulated reduced motion and a browser without View Transitions.
Preserve the product intent and already-authorized scope. Do not claim actual browser, mutation, installation or deploy execution from a reasoning-only answer.
Give an observable check and a meaningful limit; keyword presence alone is not acceptance.
acceptance: The response makes the justified decision for this raw case, provides a discriminating verification and states the evidence limits without inventing execution.
